newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile shares end firm in foreign-driven rally.
newsitem.headline: Chile shares end firm in foreign-driven rally.

text.p: Chilean shares rallied strongly for the second day in a row on a wave of foreign buying with telecom stocks among top gainers, said traders.
But the surge is likely to be short-lived with stocks stumbling at the opening as players cash in gains from the rally which has pushed blue chips up by nearly three percent, they said.
The 40-share index closed up 1.18 percent at 135.2 points. The general index firmed 0.68 percent at 5,808.31 points.
Turnover rose to 16.6 billion pesos worth of shares from 12.2 billion pesos Tuesday.

Chilean share prices rose in line with other markets in the region, bolstered by a flow of orders from Wall Street after the Federal Reserve's decision Wednesday to leave U.S. interest rates unchanged, analysts said.

"Since yesterday we have seen an interesting change in foreign flows to Latin America in general. Funds which have not traditionally been dedicated to the region are entering the market," said Guillermo Tagle, head of research at Santander Investment.
Gainers included CTC, which climbed 5.26 percent to 3,600 pesos amid speculation that the company is close to announcing a favorable merger deal with rival telecom VTR, traders said.
But Tagle said the market was too optimistic. "There are not yet sufficient grounds to see a spectacular result for CTC," he said.
Other telecom stocks that rose included Entel, up 2.98 percent to 3,110 pesos, and Telex, which gained 2.21 percent to 1,155 pesos.
Declining issues included drug-maker LabChile, off 2.59 percent at 560.10 pesos and pulp producer Copec, which shed 0.72 percent at 2,080 pesos.
